correctness.rationale: On connected supports K=N tr((L+J)^(-1))-N for J=11^T/N. The Hessian is strictly positive along a nonzero Laplacian direction and the graph is simple, so averaging over the cost-preserving automorphism group reduces the unique global solution to three orbits without imposing symmetry on competitors. In one clique the grounded matrix is uI-b11^T with u=a+mb; inverting it gives hub resistance (a+b)/(au) and leaf-pair resistance 2/u. Adding same-side and opposite-side sums with the bridge in series gives (m+1)^2/c+2(m+2)/a+4(m+1)(m-1)/u with unordered-pair normalization. For t<t_c the substituted budget wa+vu+c=B has positive coefficients; Cauchy–Schwarz gives the disclosed allocation and its u>a exactly when t<t_c. On the double star each spoke separates one vertex and each bridge side has m+1 vertices, yielding the stated S_0 allocation. An independent boundary check uses the marginal benefit N||L^+(e_i-e_j)||^2: for an active spoke it is (N-1)/a^2, and for an optional peripheral pair it is 2N/a^2 since the centered potentials are +1/a and -1/a on the two leaves only. The cost-normalized KKT inequality is therefore exactly t>=2N/(N-1), including equality and large t without assuming w>0. The proof's phrase 'forbidden b<0 side' should denote the Lagrangian derivative for increasing b from zero; the displayed sign and optimality argument are correct. The frozen finite exact and numerical sign checks are auxiliary; they do not establish all m and prices.

value.rationale: The smallest price preserving a double-star backbone is a natural design question, but this exact cutoff and all sparse allocations are already furnished by the general tree certificate.
